items.question: Is Invoiso completely free?
items.answer:
Yes — Invoiso is **100% free** and open source. No subscriptions, no hidden fees, and no premium tiers.

Download it, use it for as long as you like, and even contribute on GitHub if you want.

items.question: Does Invoiso work without an internet connection?
items.answer: Absolutely. Invoiso works **entirely offline** — all your data (customers, products, invoices) is stored right on your device. No internet connection is needed at any point.

items.question: Which operating systems does Invoiso support?
items.answer: Invoiso runs on **Windows**, **Linux**, and **macOS**. Download the installer for your platform from the GitHub Releases page.

items.question: Do I need to create an account to use Invoiso?
items.answer: No account needed. Invoiso requires **no registration**, no email address, and no sign-up of any kind — install it and start creating invoices right away.

items.question: Is my business data safe with Invoiso?
items.answer:
Your data **never leaves your device**. Invoiso stores everything in a local SQLite database — no cloud sync, no remote servers.

You're in full control, and the built-in **backup** feature keeps your data safe and portable.

items.question: How do I back up my invoice data?
items.answer:
Go to **Settings → Backup**.

Create a backup file and save it anywhere on your computer. You can restore it any time from the same screen — no internet or cloud account needed.

items.question: Can I move my data to another computer?
items.answer:
Yes. Use the **Backup** feature to export your database file, copy it to the new machine, install Invoiso there, and restore the backup from Settings.

All your customers, products, and invoices transfer completely.

items.question: Can I export invoices as PDF?
items.answer:
Yes. Generate professional PDF invoices with a single click.

Choose from three templates — **Classic**, **Modern**, and **Minimal** — and add your own logo and branding.

items.question: Does Invoiso support multiple currencies?
items.answer: Yes. Invoiso supports **USD, EUR, GBP, INR, JPY, AED, SGD, AUD, CAD**, and **JMD**. Set your preferred currency in the invoice settings.

items.question: Does Invoiso support multiple languages?
items.answer:
Yes. The app is available in **English, Hindi, Nepali, Tibetan, French, Spanish**, and **Chinese (Simplified)** — English is the default and fully reviewed.

You can also set a local-language **alias name** for each product and customer, which shows on invoice PDFs.

items.question: Can I create quotations as well as invoices?
items.answer:
Yes. When creating a document, choose either **Invoice** or **Quotation** as the type.

Both generate professional PDFs and are tracked separately in the list with color-coded badges.

items.question: Can I duplicate or clone an existing invoice?
items.answer:
Yes. Every invoice has a **Duplicate** button.

Click it, choose Invoice or Quotation, and a new document opens pre-filled with the same customer, products, tax settings, and notes — with a fresh ID and today's date. Great for repeat or recurring work.

items.question: How do I add my company logo to an invoice?
items.answer:
Go to **Settings → Company Info**, click the logo area, and choose a **PNG or JPG** image (max 512 × 512 px).

Your logo then appears automatically on every generated PDF invoice.

items.question: Can I export invoice data to CSV or Excel?
items.answer:
Yes. The **Invoice Management** screen has an **Export CSV** button in the toolbar for all your invoices, plus a **bulk export** option for just the ones you select.

The CSV opens fine in Excel, Google Sheets, or any spreadsheet app.

items.question: Does Invoiso support dark mode?
items.answer:
Yes, **dark mode** is available in beta. Go to **Settings → Company Info** and toggle it on to switch the dashboard, login screen, and core modules to a dark theme.

It's still being polished, so let us know if anything looks off.

items.question: Can I manage multiple companies or businesses in Invoiso?
items.answer:
Yes. Go to **Settings → Companies**, or tap the company name at the top of the sidebar, to create, switch between, rename, or delete companies.

Each company has its own completely separate database — invoices, customers, products, settings, and backups never mix between companies.

items.question: Why do I have to log in again after switching companies?
items.answer:
Switching companies changes which database is loaded, so Invoiso logs you out and returns to the Login screen to make sure you sign in with the right account for that company.

This also prevents data (invoices, products) that's already loaded in memory from one company leaking into the other.

items.question: Does Invoiso support GST invoicing?
items.answer: Yes. Invoiso supports **GST-ready invoices** — GSTIN fields for your company and customers, an HSN code per product, and tax rates set globally or per item. Built for Indian businesses filing GST returns.

items.question: Can I add a UPI QR code to my invoice?
items.answer:
Yes. Go to **Settings → Company Info → Payment Settings**, enter your **UPI ID** (e.g. yourname@bank), and turn on the QR toggle.

Invoiso then embeds a scannable UPI QR code in every PDF, so customers can pay instantly via GPay, PhonePe, or Paytm.

items.question: Which UPI apps work with the Invoiso QR code?
items.answer: The QR code uses the standard **upi://pay** link format, supported by all major UPI apps — **Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm, BHIM, Amazon Pay**, and any other UPI-enabled banking app.

items.question: Is Invoiso available as a portable version?
items.answer:
The **Linux** build is a portable **AppImage** — no installation needed. Download the file, mark it executable, and run it.

The **Windows** build uses a standard installer.

items.question: Where is my data stored on disk?
items.answer:
Your database lives in your OS's app-data folder — typically **~/.local/share/invoiso/** on Linux, and **%AppData%\anoopp\invoiso\** on Windows.

In debug mode, the exact path is also shown on the splash screen at startup.

items.question: What do I do if I forgot my password?
items.answer: Use the built-in self-service reset — no reinstalling and no losing your invoices, customers, or data. Click "Forgot password?" on the login screen, then copy the **Installation ID** shown there and send it to support. Support will send back a **one-time response code**; enter that code in the app and set a new password, and you're back in.

items.question: Is the source code available?
items.answer: Yes. Invoiso is fully **open source** under the **MIT license**. The complete source code is on GitHub — contributions, bug reports, and feature requests are all welcome.

items.question: Is Invoiso a free alternative to Vyapar?
items.answer:
Yes. Invoiso is a free, open-source alternative to **Vyapar** for Windows, Linux, and macOS.

Unlike Vyapar, Invoiso needs **no account or phone signup**, is completely free with **no paid tier**, and is open source under the MIT license. Both apps support offline billing and GST-ready invoices with UPI QR codes — but Invoiso also runs on **Linux and macOS**, which Vyapar doesn't.

items.question: Can I use Invoiso as free GST billing software for my business in India?
items.answer:
Yes. Invoiso works well as **free GST billing software** for Indian businesses — GSTIN fields, HSN codes, **CGST/SGST/IGST** tax rates, and UPI QR payments on PDFs, all generated entirely offline.

No subscription, no account, no internet required.

items.question: Which types of businesses in India use Invoiso?
items.answer:
All kinds — **kirana shops, retailers, hardware stores, textile sellers, traders, wholesalers**, service businesses, repair shops, freelancers, consultants, and agencies.

If you need offline GST billing, PDF invoices, and payment tracking without a subscription, Invoiso fits.

items.question: Can Invoiso track UPI ↔ cash exchanges and service fees?
items.answer:
Yes. Turn on **Cash Exchange Services** in **Settings → Accessibility → Optional features**.

Record **UPI → Cash** and **Cash → UPI** exchanges with a separate **service fee** (only the fee counts as income), plus expenses, withdrawals and bank deposits. Invoiso keeps your **Cash** and **UPI/Bank** balances up to date — including invoice payments — and can print or download a receipt when a customer asks.

Admins also see each day's net **Cash** and **UPI/Bank** in **Reports → Daily Report**. Staff can record entries but don't see balances or service income.

items.question: Can I hide purchase price and profit from my staff?
items.answer:
Yes. In **Settings → Product Columns**, turn on **Purchase Price: Admins Only**.

Staff (non-admin users) can still see products, selling prices and available stock, but **not** the purchase price, cost, profit or stock value. Admins see everything.

items.question: Can I stop staff from changing stock or opening Reports and Purchase Bills?
items.answer:
Yes. All of these are off by default:

- **Settings → Product Columns → Stock Editing: Admins Only**: staff can't set or change stock quantities, and can't import products from CSV. Invoices still update stock automatically.
- **Settings → Accessibility → Reports: Admins Only**: the **Reports** menu is hidden from staff.
- **Settings → Accessibility → Purchase Bills & Suppliers: Admins Only**: the **Purchase Bills** and **Suppliers** menus are hidden from staff (shown once Purchase Bills & Suppliers is turned on).

items.question: Can I set a different low-stock alert level for each product?
items.answer:
Yes. Set a **Low-stock limit** on any product (blank uses the default of **10**).

Products at or below their limit appear in the **Low Stock** tab and in the dashboard **Low Stock** alert.

items.question: Can I mark an invoice as paid while creating it?
items.answer: Yes. The create-invoice screen has a **Payment** section — choose **Paid**, **Partial** or **Unpaid**, the payment method (Cash, UPI, Bank Transfer…) and the amount. The payment is recorded when you save.

items.question: Can I record purchases from my suppliers and add the stock?
items.answer:
Yes. Turn on **Settings → Accessibility → Purchase Bills & Suppliers** — this adds **Purchase Bills** and **Suppliers** to the menu.

1. Open **Purchase Bills** and click **New Purchase Bill**.
2. Pick a saved supplier, or choose **Walk-in Supplier** and type a name.
3. Add the products with quantity and cost, then click **Save Purchase Bill**.

The quantities are **added to stock** as soon as the bill is saved, and each product's purchase price is updated to the cost on its latest bill. Use **Apply Payment** on the bill to record what you paid — the supplier's **Outstanding** shows what you still owe.

items.question: How do I take back goods a customer returned?
items.answer:
On the **Invoices** (or **Receipts**) screen, click **⋮** on the invoice and choose **Return Items**. A form opens with each line set to the quantity that can still be returned (**Left**).

1. Reduce or remove the lines that didn't come back.
2. Tick **To stock** on lines going back on the shelf. Leave it unticked for damaged goods.
3. Under **Settlement**, choose how to settle: **Reduce invoice balance** (only when the invoice is still unpaid), **Refund now** (pick Cash, UPI…) or **Keep as customer credit**.
4. Save. Invoiso creates a numbered **credit note** and updates stock and balances.

You can't return more than was sold — each line is capped at what's left. When **Credit / Debit Notes (advanced)** is on, the menu item is called **Create Credit Note (Sales Return)**.

items.question: Does Invoiso support credit notes and debit notes?
items.answer:
Yes. A **credit note** is created every time you return items from an invoice (**⋮ → Return Items**) — that works out of the box.

For more, turn on **Settings → Accessibility → Credit / Debit Notes (advanced)**. It adds:

- **Credit Notes** and **Debit Notes** screens that list every note.
- **Create Debit Note** on an invoice — use it to charge the customer extra after the invoice, for example a price revision or a missed charge. A debit note adds to what the customer owes and doesn't change stock.
- Notes that aren't linked to any invoice.
- Your own number prefixes in **Settings → Invoice Settings** (**Credit note prefix**, **Debit note prefix**). Notes have their own number sequence.

Notes print as PDFs just like invoices.

items.question: Can I keep a refund as customer credit and use it later?
items.answer:
Yes. When you return items, choose **Keep as customer credit** under **Settlement**. The amount is saved for that customer.

To use it later:

- **On a new invoice:** in the **Payment** section, tick **Apply customer credit to this invoice**. It covers up to the amount still owed.
- **On an existing invoice:** on the invoice row, click **⋮ → Apply customer credit**.
- **Pay it back as money:** on the **Credit Notes** screen, click **⋮ → Refund** on the note. You can then print a **Refund voucher** for the customer. (The Credit Notes screen needs **Credit / Debit Notes (advanced)** turned on in Accessibility.)

items.question: Can I save an invoice as a draft and finish it later?
items.answer:
Yes. Click **Save Draft** at the bottom of the create screen. A draft:

- has **no invoice number** yet — the header only previews the number it's likely to get,
- **doesn't reduce stock**,
- doesn't count in reports, balances or payments,
- shows a **DRAFT** badge in the list,
- can be checked with **PDF Preview** (the number shows as **DRAFT**), but can't be downloaded or printed until it's finalized.

To finish it, click **Edit** on the draft, make your changes and click **Finalize** (for example **Finalize Invoice**). That gives it the next number, reduces stock and records any payment chosen in the **Payment** section. If the draft is dated before today, Invoiso asks whether to keep that date or use today's, so numbers stay in date order.

Drafts work the same way for receipts, quotations and credit/debit notes. A purchase bill draft doesn't add stock until you open it and click **Save Purchase Bill**.

items.question: How do I cancel a wrong invoice or receipt?
items.answer:
Use **Cancel / Void**, not Trash. On the **Invoices** or **Receipts** screen, click **⋮ → Cancel / Void** on the row.

- Keep **Return all items to stock** ticked if the goods came back. Untick it if they didn't (damaged, used or kept by the customer).
- The invoice stays in the list marked **Declined**, keeps its number, and no longer counts in reports or balances.
- It can't be edited or undone afterwards.

Cancel / Void isn't available while the invoice has payments recorded (delete them in **Apply Payment** first) or has credit or debit notes, including drafts (cancel or trash those first). To take back only part of a sale, use **⋮ → Return Items** instead.

items.question: Why didn't the stock come back when I moved an invoice to trash?
items.answer:
Moving an invoice or receipt to **Trash** only hides it — it never changes stock, and restoring it doesn't either. To cancel a sale and put the goods back into stock, use **⋮ → Cancel / Void** (see *How do I cancel a wrong invoice or receipt?*).

Purchase bills are different: moving a saved purchase bill to trash takes its quantities back out of stock, and restoring it adds them again.

items.question: Can I show amounts with commas, like 1,00,000.00?
items.answer:
Yes. Go to **Settings → Invoice Settings → Number format** (just below Date format), pick a style and click **Save**:

- **No separator** — 1234567.89
- **International** — 1,234,567.89
- **Indian** — 12,34,567.89

It applies to invoice and receipt PDFs, payment receipts, refund vouchers, customer statements and amounts shown on screen. Fields where you type amounts, CSV exports and the UPI QR code always use plain numbers.

New setups start with **Indian** for INR and **International** for other currencies. Existing setups keep **No separator** until you change it.

items.question: Can I record a customer's age, date of birth, gender or a separate shipping address?
items.answer:
Yes. Go to **Settings → Invoice Settings → Customer Fields** and turn on what you need:

- **Separate Shipping Address** — a Ship To name, phone and address. If it's the same as billing, only one address prints.
- **Date of Birth** — the age is worked out from it.
- **Age** — used only when no date of birth is entered.
- **Gender** — Male, Female or Other.
- **Customer Custom Fields** — up to 5 of your own fields, like Patient ID or Blood Group.

Each field has its own **Print on PDF** switch. Once turned on, the fields appear on the customer form and on the create-invoice screen.

items.question: Can I add a new product while creating an invoice or purchase bill?
items.answer:
Yes. Click **New product** next to the product search (on the create-invoice screen it's beside **Custom item**). It's the same form as adding a product in **Products**, with the same rules — for example, staff can't set stock if stock editing is admin-only. Whatever you typed in the search box becomes the name.

When you save, the product is added to your catalogue **and** straight onto the invoice or bill. If a product with the same name already exists, Invoiso asks before creating another.

**On a purchase bill**, the product's **Stock** field means stock you already had *before* this bill — saving the bill adds the bought quantity on top. For stock you're buying now, leave Stock at 0 and enter the quantity on the bill.

items.question: Why do I get a "Not enough stock" message when I save?
items.answer:
When you save, update or finalize an invoice or receipt, Invoiso checks the current stock again. If any product would go below zero — for example because another sale used the stock after you started — it lists each one with **in stock**, **on invoice** and **short by**.

- **Go back** — change the quantities.
- **Save anyway** — save it; stock for those products goes below zero.

Quotations, credit/debit notes and drafts aren't checked, because they don't take stock. Services and products with unlimited stock are never short.
